wanga-kingdom.t: The only centralised kingdom among the Luhya of western Kenya, whose king Mumia became a key ally of British colonial expansion.
wanga-kingdom.o: Wanga traditions say the kingdom was founded around the mid-17th century by Wanga, a prince who had migrated from the area of Tiriki or further west and established a royal line among the [[e:luhya-people|Luhya]] of the [[e:mumias|Mumias]] area. The capital lay at Elureko, near today's Mumias.
wanga-kingdom.r: The nabongo (king) ruled with clan elders and a royal council over a farming people, and used alliances with [[e:maasai-people|Maasai]] and [[e:kalenjin-people|Kalenjin]] warriors to raid and dominate neighbours. In the 19th century [[e:swahili|Swahili]] and Arab caravans used Wanga as a base. [[e:nabongo-mumia|Nabongo Mumia]] (r. 1882 to 1949) welcomed the [[s:imperial-british-east-africa-company|Imperial British East Africa Company]] and helped British expansion across western [[s:kenya|Kenya]].
wanga-kingdom.e: The British made [[e:nabongo-mumia|Mumia]] paramount chief of much of western [[s:kenya|Kenya]], but in 1926 his authority was reduced to an honorary position, ending Wanga's role as a governing kingdom. The town of [[e:mumias|Mumias]] bears his name, and the title of nabongo survives as a cultural office.

western-yan.t: A wandering Murong Xianbei state born in the Former Qin collapse, which sacked Chang'an and then settled in Shanxi until Later Yan destroyed it in 394.
western-yan.o: After [[s:former-qin|Former Qin]]'s defeat at the [[e:battle-of-fei-river|Fei River]] in 383, [[e:murong-xianbei|Murong]] Hong, a prince of the deposed [[s:former-yan|Former Yan]] house, rebelled in 384 near [[e:changan|Chang'an]], where many [[s:xianbei|Xianbei]] had been resettled. His brother [[e:murong-chong|Murong Chong]] took over, captured and plundered Chang'an in 385 and proclaimed himself emperor.
western-yan.r: Western Yan was less a settled state than a migrating host of [[s:xianbei|Xianbei]] soldiers and families, longing to return east. Its leaders were murdered in quick succession by their own followers. In 386 the host moved into [[e:shanxi|Shanxi]], where [[e:murong-yong|Murong Yong]] established himself at [[e:changzi|Changzi]].
western-yan.e: [[e:murong-yong|Murong Yong]] refused to submit to his relative [[e:murong-chui|Murong Chui of Later Yan]], who regarded himself as the rightful heir of the Yan line. In 394 [[e:murong-xianbei|Murong]] Chui invaded, took [[e:changzi|Changzi]] and executed Murong Yong.

western-chagatai-khanate.t: The Transoxianan half of the divided Chagatai Khanate, ruled in practice by Turkic amirs and the springboard for Timur's rise.
western-chagatai-khanate.o: The [[e:chagatai-khanate|Chagatai Khanate]] split in the 1340s. In the west, the [[s:qaraunas|Qara'unas]] amir [[e:qazaghan|Qazaghan]] defeated and killed Khan [[e:qazan-khan-ibn-yasaur|Qazan]] in 1346 or 1347, after which [[e:transoxiana|Transoxiana]] was governed by [[e:amir|amirs]] who set up puppet khans of Chagatai or Ögedei descent, while the east became [[s:moghulistan|Moghulistan]].
western-chagatai-khanate.r: Real power lay with the Turkic and Mongol tribal [[e:amir|amirs]] of the [[e:barlas|Barlas]], [[e:jalairs|Jalayir]], Arlat and [[s:qaraunas|Qara'unas]], who had settled among the towns of [[e:transoxiana|Transoxiana]] and adopted [[e:islam|Islam]]. [[e:qazaghan|Qazaghan]] ruled as amir until his murder in 1358, after which rival amirs fought for control. The region was invaded twice by [[e:tughlugh-timur|Tughlugh Timur]] of [[s:moghulistan|Moghulistan]], in 1360 and 1361.
western-chagatai-khanate.e: Out of these struggles rose [[e:timur|Timur]] of the [[e:barlas|Barlas]], first allied with and then against [[e:amir-husayn|Amir Husayn]], [[e:qazaghan|Qazaghan's]] grandson. In 1370 Timur defeated Husayn at [[e:balkh|Balkh]] and took power, ruling through a puppet Chagatai khan and founding the [[s:timurid-empire|Timurid Empire]].

wanaparthy-samasthan.t: A Telugu-country estate of the Reddy Rajas of Wanaparthy, one of the leading samasthans holding land under the Nizams of Hyderabad.
wanaparthy-samasthan.o: The Rajas of Wanaparthy, of the Janampally family, established themselves in the region south of [[e:hyderabad|Hyderabad]] in the early 16th century; the register's date follows family tradition. They later held their estate as a samasthan, a tributary chiefship within [[s:hyderabad-state|Hyderabad State]].
wanaparthy-samasthan.r: The Rajas paid tribute to the Nizam but ran their own revenue and courts. Successive rulers took the name Rameshwar Rao and supported [[e:telugu-language|Telugu]] and [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] learning. They built the palace at Wanaparthy, later used as a college.
wanaparthy-samasthan.e: After Hyderabad was integrated into [[e:india|India]] in 1948, the samasthan's powers ended. The family's J. Rameshwar Rao later served as a member of the Indian Parliament. Wanaparthy is now a district of [[e:telangana|Telangana]].

wabanaki-confederacy.t: An alliance of Algonquian peoples of northern New England and the Maritimes, the People of the Dawnland, long allied with New France against the English.
wabanaki-confederacy.o: The [[e:abenaki|Abenaki]], [[e:penobscot|Penobscot]], [[e:passamaquoddy|Passamaquoddy]], [[e:maliseet|Maliseet]] and [[e:mikmaq|Mi'kmaq]] shared related languages and ties of kinship and trade. In the later 17th century, facing [[s:mohawk-nation|Mohawk]] raids and English expansion after [[e:king-philips-war|King Philip's War]], they formalised an alliance, often dated to around 1680, with a council fire linked to the Catholic mission villages of the [[e:st-lawrence-river|St Lawrence]].
wabanaki-confederacy.r: Each nation kept its own sachems and territories, while the confederacy coordinated diplomacy and war through councils and wampum. Hunting, fishing, gathering and some [[e:maize|maize]] farming supported communities from the [[e:merrimack-river|Merrimack]] to [[s:colony-of-cape-breton-island|Cape Breton]]. Allied with [[s:new-france|New France]] and supported by missionaries such as [[e:sebastien-rale|Sébastien Rale]], the Wabanaki fought the English in a series of wars from 1688, including [[e:dummers-war|Father Rale's War]] in 1722 to 1725. Leaders such as the [[e:penobscot|Penobscot]] sachem [[e:madockawando|Madockawando]] dealt with both empires.
wabanaki-confederacy.e: After the fall of [[s:new-france|New France]] the nations signed Peace and Friendship Treaties with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]]. The confederacy gradually lapsed and was formally dissolved in 1862, but it was revived in 1993.

western-chalukya-empire.t: The Deccan empire of the Chalukyas of Kalyani, rival of the Cholas, whose reign saw a golden age of Kannada literature and ornate temple building.
western-chalukya-empire.o: In 973 [[e:tailapa-ii|Tailapa II]], a feudatory of the [[s:rashtrakuta-dynasty|Rashtrakuta dynasty]] claiming descent from the [[s:chalukyas-of-badami|Chalukyas of Badami]], overthrew [[e:karka-ii|Karka II]] and restored [[e:chalukya-dynasty|Chalukya]] rule over the western [[e:deccan|Deccan]]. He defeated the Paramara king [[e:vakpati-munja|Vakpati Munja]], and his successors fought a long war with the [[s:chola-empire|Chola Empire]] for the [[e:raichur|Raichur]] doab and [[e:vengi|Vengi]].
western-chalukya-empire.r: [[e:someshvara-i|Someshvara I]] made [[e:basavakalyan|Kalyani]], modern Basavakalyan, the capital. [[e:vikramaditya-vi|Vikramaditya VI]], who ruled from 1076 to 1126, started a new era and was celebrated in [[e:bilhana|Bilhana's]] [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] biography; the jurist [[e:vijnaneshvara|Vijnaneshvara]] wrote the [[e:mitakshara|Mitakshara]], a commentary on [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] law, at his court. The empire's ornate temples, at [[e:lakkundi|Lakkundi]], [[e:itagi|Itagi]] and [[e:gadag|Gadag]], and its [[e:kannada|Kannada]] literature mark a creative peak, supported by trading [[e:guild|guilds]] such as the [[e:ainnurruvar|Ainnurruvar]].
western-chalukya-empire.e: In 1162 the Kalachuri minister [[e:bijjala-ii|Bijjala]] seized power, and during his rule the [[e:lingayatism|Lingayat]] reform of [[e:basava|Basava]] began. [[e:someshvara-iv|Someshvara IV]] briefly restored the dynasty in 1184, but by 1189 its lands were divided between the [[s:hoysala-empire|Hoysala Empire]] and the [[e:seuna-yadava-dynasty|Yadavas]].

west-francia.t: Western third of the Carolingian realm, created at Verdun in 843, out of which the Kingdom of France grew.
west-francia.o: After civil war among the sons of [[e:louis-the-pious|Louis the Pious]], the [[e:treaty-of-verdun|Treaty of Verdun]] in 843 gave [[e:charles-the-bald|Charles the Bald]] the lands west of the [[e:scheldt|Scheldt]], [[e:meuse|Meuse]], [[e:saone|Saône]] and [[e:rhone|Rhône]]. His realm took in [[s:neustria|Neustria]], [[s:duchy-of-aquitaine|Aquitaine]], [[e:gascony|Gascony]] and the [[s:marca-hispanica|Spanish March]], though [[s:duchy-of-brittany|Brittany]] remained largely independent.
west-francia.r: Royal power weakened under the pressure of [[e:vikings|Viking]] raids and of great regional [[e:magnates|magnates]] who turned their offices into hereditary principalities. [[e:charles-the-bald|Charles the Bald]] ordered fortified bridges in the [[e:edict-of-pitres|Edict of Pîtres]] in 864. Count [[e:odo-of-france|Odo of Paris]] defended the city against the Vikings in 885 to 886 and was elected king, beginning a rivalry between [[e:carolingian-empire|Carolingians]] and his Robertian family.
west-francia.e: In 911 [[e:charles-the-simple|Charles the Simple]] granted [[e:rollo|Rollo]] the land that became the [[s:duchy-of-normandy|Duchy of Normandy]]. Kings alternated between the two families until the last Carolingian, Louis V, died in 987, when the [[e:magnates|magnates]] elected [[e:hugh-capet|Hugh Capet]], founding the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]].

wari-empire.t: The first expansionist state of the Andean highlands, which built a network of administrative centres and roads across Peru centuries before the Incas.
wari-empire.o: Wari arose around 600 CE in the [[e:ayacucho|Ayacucho]] basin of the central Peruvian highlands, drawing on the local [[e:huarpa-culture|Huarpa culture]] and religious imagery shared with [[s:tiwanaku|Tiwanaku]]. Its capital, Wari, grew into a city of perhaps 40,000 people covering several square kilometres.
wari-empire.r: From its capital Wari established planned provincial centres such as [[e:pikillacta|Pikillacta]] near [[e:cusco|Cusco]], [[e:viracochapampa|Viracochapampa]] in the north and [[e:cerro-baul|Cerro Baúl]] in [[e:moquegua|Moquegua]], facing [[s:tiwanaku|Tiwanaku]]. These rectangular compounds suggest a centralised administration that controlled labour and goods. Wari built terraces and roads that the [[e:inca-empire|Incas]] later reused, and may have used early khipus for records. Its tapestry tunics and colourful pottery spread a common style. Tombs at [[e:el-castillo-de-huarmey|El Castillo de Huarmey]] show the wealth of Wari noblewomen.
wari-empire.e: The Wari state broke up around 1000, perhaps owing to drought and internal conflict, and its centres were abandoned. Its administrative model and roads influenced later states, notably the [[s:inca-empire|Inca Empire]], while regional powers such as the [[s:chanka-confederation|Chanka Confederation]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-chimor|Kingdom of Chimor]] rose in its wake.

western-satraps.t: Saka rulers of western India for nearly four centuries, whose king Rudradaman left the first long royal inscription in Sanskrit.
western-satraps.o: The Western Satraps were [[s:saka|Saka]] governors who, under the [[s:kushan-empire|Kushan Empire]] or independently, built a state in [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]], [[e:malwa|Malwa]] and [[e:sindh|Sindh]] in the 1st century. The first line, the [[e:kshaharata-dynasty|Kshaharatas]], reached its height under [[e:nahapana|Nahapana]]. A second line, the [[e:kardamaka-dynasty|Kardamakas]], was founded by [[e:chastana|Chastana]] in [[e:ujjain|Ujjain]] and became the main dynasty.
western-satraps.r: They controlled the rich port of [[e:bharuch|Bharuch]] and the trade routes to [[e:ujjain|Ujjain]]. Their [[e:silver|silver]] coins, dated in the [[e:saka-era|Saka era]] from 78, give an unusually exact chronology. [[e:rudradaman-i|Rudradaman I's]] [[s:junagadh-state|Junagadh]] inscription of 150 boasts of his victories over the [[s:satavahana-dynasty|Satavahana dynasty]] and the [[s:yaudheya-republic|Yaudheyas]] and of repairing the [[e:sudarshana-lake|Sudarshana]] reservoir, and is written in elegant [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]], a sign of its spread as a courtly language.
western-satraps.e: After long rivalry with the Satavahanas, the [[e:satrapy|satraps]] declined in the 4th century. Around 395 to 415 the Gupta emperor [[e:chandragupta-ii|Chandragupta II]] defeated the last ruler, [[e:rudrasimha-iii|Rudrasimha III]], and annexed [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] and [[e:malwa|Malwa]], opening the western ports to the [[s:gupta-empire|Gupta Empire]].

western-wei-206-bc.t: Wei Bao's kingdom in southern Shanxi, one of the Eighteen Kingdoms of 206 BCE, conquered by Han Xin's surprise crossing of the Yellow River.
western-wei-206-bc.o: [[e:wei-bao|Wei Bao]], of the royal house of the old [[s:state-of-wei|State of Wei]], had been made King of Wei during the rising against the [[s:qin-dynasty|Qin dynasty]]. In [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu's]] settlement of 206 BCE he lost the Wei heartland around [[e:kaifeng|Daliang]] and was moved west to rule as King of [[s:western-wei|Western Wei]] from [[e:pingyang-shanxi|Pingyang]] in the [[e:fen-river|Fen]] valley of [[e:shanxi|Shanxi]].
western-wei-206-bc.r: The kingdom covered the [[e:hedong-shanxi|Hedong]] region, rich in salt and grain, on the east bank of the [[e:yellow-river|Yellow River]] facing the [[e:guanzhong|Guanzhong]] region. It was a frontline state whose loyalty swung with the fortunes of Chu and Han.
western-wei-206-bc.e: [[e:wei-bao|Wei Bao]] joined [[e:liu-bang|Liu Bang]] in 205 BCE, then deserted him after the Han defeat at [[e:xuzhou|Pengcheng]]. That autumn [[e:han-xin|Han Xin]] feinted at one ford while crossing at Xiayang on rafts of wooden jars, and captured Wei Bao. His concubine [[e:empress-dowager-bo|Bo Ji]] later bore Liu Bang a son, the future [[e:emperor-wen-of-han|Emperor Wen of Han]].

wang-jingwei-regime.t: The collaborationist government that the veteran Kuomintang leader Wang Jingwei set up at Nanjing in 1940 under Japanese protection.
wang-jingwei-regime.o: [[e:wang-jingwei|Wang Jingwei]], a close associate of [[e:sun-yat-sen|Sun Yat-sen]] and rival of [[e:chiang-kai-shek|Chiang Kai-shek]], believed [[e:china|China]] could not win the war against [[e:japan|Japan]]. He fled [[e:chongqing|Chongqing]] in December 1938 and, after negotiations with Japan, inaugurated a 'reorganised' National Government at [[e:nanjing|Nanjing]] on 30 March 1940, absorbing the [[s:provisional-government-of-the-republic-of-china|Provisional Government of the Republic of China]] and the [[s:reformed-government-of-the-republic-of-china|Reformed Government of the Republic of China]].
wang-jingwei-regime.r: The regime used the name, flag and symbols of the [[s:nationalist-government|Nationalist government]], claiming to be its legitimate continuation. [[e:japan|Japan]] recognised it in 1940, and in 1943 it declared war on [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and the [[s:united-states|United States]] and took over the [[s:shanghai-international-settlement|Shanghai International Settlement]] and the [[s:shanghai-french-concession|Shanghai French Concession]]. In practice Japanese armies controlled it, and Wang's officials, among them [[e:chen-gongbo|Chen Gongbo]] and [[e:zhou-fohai|Zhou Fohai]], had limited room for action.
wang-jingwei-regime.e: [[e:wang-jingwei|Wang Jingwei]] died in [[e:japan|Japan]] in November 1944, and [[e:chen-gongbo|Chen Gongbo]] succeeded him. The regime dissolved after Japan surrendered in August 1945. Its leaders were tried as traitors, and Chen Gongbo was executed in 1946.

water-chenla.t: The southern, lowland half of divided Chenla in the 8th century, a fragmented Khmer realm of the Mekong plains and delta.
water-chenla.o: After the death of [[e:jayavarman-i|Jayavarman I]] around 681, [[s:chenla|Chenla]] lost its unity, and Chinese records from about 707 distinguish a southern Water Chenla, Shui Zhenla, from [[s:land-chenla|Land Chenla]]. It covered the lower [[e:mekong-river|Mekong]], the [[e:tonle-sap|Tonle Sap]] region and the delta, the old lands of [[s:funan|Funan]].
water-chenla.r: Water [[s:chenla|Chenla]] appears to have been divided among several rulers, including a queen Jayadevi known from an inscription of 713 who complained of hard times. Centres such as [[e:sambhupura|Sambhupura]], near Sambor on the [[e:mekong-river|Mekong]], and Aninditapura held local power. Its kings followed Shaivite cults and wrote in [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] and [[e:old-khmer|Old Khmer]].
water-chenla.e: In the late 8th century Javanese raids, possibly from the [[e:sailendra-dynasty|Sailendra]] kingdom, struck the region. [[e:jayavarman-ii|Jayavarman II]], who had spent time in [[e:java|Java]], returned to unite the [[e:khmer-empire|Khmer]] lands and in 802 proclaimed himself universal monarch, ending the division and founding the [[s:khmer-empire|Khmer Empire]].

wusun.t: Nomads of the Ili valley and Issyk-Kul who became the Han dynasty's chief steppe ally against the Xiongnu, sealed by marriages to Chinese princesses.
wusun.o: The Wusun first lived near the [[s:yuezhi|Yuezhi]] in the [[e:gansu|Gansu]] region and were subject to the [[e:xiongnu-empire|Xiongnu]]. Their ruler, the kunmo [[e:liejiaomi|Liejiaomi]], raised by the Xiongnu, led them west around 161 BCE to the Ili valley and the [[e:issyk-kul|Issyk-Kul]] basin, driving out the [[e:yuezhi|Yuezhi]] and the [[s:saka|Saka]] who had settled there.
wusun.r: The Han envoy [[e:zhang-qian|Zhang Qian]] visited around 115 BCE seeking an alliance. The Wusun were pastoralists with large horse herds and, by Han count, some 630,000 people, ruled by the kunmo from the Red Valley city of [[e:chigu|Chigu]]. Han princesses, including [[e:liu-xijun|Liu Xijun]], who wrote a famous lament on her exile, married Wusun rulers, and in 71 BCE a joint Han-Wusun campaign struck the [[e:xiongnu-empire|Xiongnu]]. A [[e:dual-kingship|dual kingship]] of greater and lesser kunmo developed after 53 BCE.
wusun.e: The Wusun weakened through internal division and pressure from the [[s:rouran-khaganate|Rouran Khaganate]], moving into the [[e:pamir-mountains|Pamirs]] in the 5th century, after which they disappear as a distinct power. Their remnants merged into later [[e:turkic-peoples|Turkic peoples]] of the [[e:semirechye|Zhetysu]] region.

wallis-and-futuna.t: A French Pacific territory of two island groups where three traditional kings still share authority with the French state.
wallis-and-futuna.o: [[s:kingdom-of-uvea|Wallis]] was the seat of the Kingdom of Uvea, ruled by the [[e:lavelua|Lavelua]], and [[e:futuna-wallis-and-futuna|Futuna]] was divided between the kingdoms of [[e:kingdom-of-sigave|Sigave]] and [[e:kingdom-of-alo|Alo]]. [[e:society-of-mary-marists|Marist]] missionaries arrived in 1837; on Futuna the priest [[e:pierre-chanel|Pierre Chanel]] was killed in 1841 and later canonised. [[e:amelia-tokagahahau-aliki|Queen Amelia of Uvea]] signed a [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] treaty with [[e:france|France]] in 1887, and the Futuna kings followed in 1888.
wallis-and-futuna.r: The [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] was administered from [[s:new-caledonia|New Caledonia]], and the Catholic Church held great influence over schooling and daily life, while the kings kept customary authority over land and local justice. The islands lived by subsistence farming and fishing. During the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]] [[s:kingdom-of-uvea|Wallis]] hosted an American base. Many islanders emigrated to New [[s:new-caledonia-darien|Caledonia]] for work.
wallis-and-futuna.e: After a referendum in 1959, Wallis and [[e:futuna-wallis-and-futuna|Futuna]] became a French overseas territory in 1961 and an overseas collectivity in 2003. The three kings remain recognised in its statute, and more Wallisians and Futunans now live in [[s:new-caledonia|New Caledonia]] than at home.

wild-and-rhinegraviate.t: A county on the Nahe and in the Hunsrück whose Wild- and Rhinegraves, ancestors of the princes of Salm, ruled from castles above Kirn.
wild-and-rhinegraviate.o: The Wildgraves held lands in the [[e:hunsruck|Hunsrück]] and on the [[e:nahe|Nahe]], while the Rhinegraves ruled around [[e:rheingrafenstein|Rheingrafenstein]]. In 1409 the Rhinegrave John III inherited the Wildgraviate, uniting both titles as Wild- and Rhinegraves. A marriage in 1475 later brought them half of the county of Salm in the [[e:vosges|Vosges]].
wild-and-rhinegraviate.r: The family repeatedly divided its lands into branches such as [[e:dhaun-castle|Dhaun]], [[e:kyrburg|Kyrburg]] and Grumbach, with Kyrburg castle above [[e:kirn|Kirn]] as a main seat. Most branches became Lutheran, though some Salm lines returned to [[e:catholicism|Catholicism]]. The counts often served as officers in French and imperial armies, and branches were raised to princes as [[s:principality-of-salm|Salm-Salm]] and [[s:principality-of-salm-1802|Salm-Kyrburg]] in the 17th and 18th centuries.
wild-and-rhinegraviate.e: [[e:french-revolutionary-occupation-of-the-netherlands|French revolutionary armies]] occupied the left bank of the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] in 1794, ending the family's rule there. Compensated in 1803 with secularised lands in [[e:westphalia|Westphalia]], the princes of Salm formed the [[s:principality-of-salm|Principality of Salm]], which [[e:france|France]] annexed in 1811.

wuyue.t: A peaceful and prosperous coastal kingdom around Hangzhou, famous for its Buddhist pagodas and sea trade, that handed itself over to the Song without a fight.
wuyue.o: [[e:qian-liu|Qian Liu]], a former salt smuggler who became a soldier, defeated the rebel [[e:dong-chang|Dong Chang]] in 896 and gained control of the [[e:zhejiang|Zhejiang]] coast. In 907 the [[s:later-liang|Later Liang]] named him Prince of Wuyue, and he governed from Qiantang (modern [[e:hangzhou|Hangzhou]]).
wuyue.r: The Qian rulers generally accepted the suzerainty of the northern dynasties, avoiding major wars except with their neighbour [[s:wu-ten-kingdoms|Wu (Ten Kingdoms)]] and its successor [[s:southern-tang|Southern Tang]]. They built sea walls along the [[e:qiantang-river|Qiantang river]], drained and irrigated land, and traded by sea with the Khitan, [[e:korea|Korea]] and [[e:japan|Japan]]. Wuyue was a great centre of [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]], and the [[e:leifeng-pagoda|Leifeng]] and [[e:baochu-pagoda|Baochu]] pagodas of [[e:hangzhou|Hangzhou]] date from its rule.
wuyue.e: [[e:qian-chu|Qian Chu]], the last king, helped the [[s:song-dynasty|Song Dynasty]] conquer [[s:southern-tang|Southern Tang]] and in 978 surrendered his whole kingdom to [[e:song-dynasty|Song]] without bloodshed. The Qian family was honoured at the Song court, and [[e:hangzhou|Hangzhou]] later became the [[s:southern-song|Southern Song]] capital.

western-chu.t: The kingdom of Xiang Yu, Hegemon-King of Western Chu, who destroyed the Qin armies and redrew China's map, only to lose it all to Liu Bang at Gaixia in 202 BCE.
western-chu.o: [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu]], grandson of the Chu general [[e:xiang-yan|Xiang Yan]], rose with his uncle Xiang [[s:state-of-wei|Liang]] in the rebellion against the [[s:qin-dynasty|Qin dynasty]]. After his victory at [[e:battle-of-julu|Julu]] in 207 BCE he took [[e:xianyang|Xianyang]], killed the surrendered [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin]] ruler [[e:ziying|Ziying]] and burned the palaces. In 206 BCE he divided the empire into eighteen kingdoms and took for himself the title of Hegemon-King of Western Chu, ruling from [[e:xuzhou|Pengcheng]] (Xuzhou).
western-chu.r: Western Chu held nine [[e:commandery|commanderies]] of the old [[s:state-of-chu|State of Chu]] and the [[s:state-of-wei|State of Wei]]. [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu]] dominated the other kings by military force, but he alienated allies, had his nominal sovereign [[e:emperor-yi-of-chu|Emperor Yi of Chu]] killed in 205 BCE and treated defeated enemies brutally. His crushing victory over [[e:liu-bang|Liu Bang]] at [[e:xuzhou|Pengcheng]] was never turned into lasting advantage.
western-chu.e: Over four years of [[e:chu-han-contention|Chu-Han war]], [[e:liu-bang|Liu Bang's]] alliances wore Western Chu down. Surrounded at [[e:battle-of-gaixia|Gaixia]] in 202 BCE and hearing Chu songs from the enemy camp, [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu]] broke out and killed himself by the Wu River. Liu Bang then founded the [[s:han-dynasty|Han Dynasty]].

wu-ten-kingdoms.t: The first of the southern Ten Kingdoms, ruled from Yangzhou by the Yang family and their powerful ministers, which became the basis of Southern Tang.
wu-ten-kingdoms.o: [[e:yang-xingmi|Yang Xingmi]], a soldier of humble origins, won control of the Huainan region between the Huai and [[e:yangtze-river|Yangtze]] rivers in the 890s and made [[e:yangzhou|Yangzhou]] his base. The [[s:later-tang|Tang]] named him Prince of Wu in 902, and after the dynasty fell in 907 his family refused to recognise the [[s:later-liang|Later Liang]].
wu-ten-kingdoms.r: Wu was rich from salt production and [[e:yangtze-river|Yangtze]] trade, and fought repeated wars with [[s:wuyue|Wuyue]] and the northern dynasties. [[e:yang-xingmi|Yang Xingmi's]] sons were weak, and real power passed to the general [[e:xu-wen|Xu Wen]] and his adopted son [[e:li-bian|Xu Zhigao]], who ran the government from [[e:nanjing|Jinling]] (Nanjing). [[e:yang-pu|Yang Pu]] took the title of emperor in 927.
wu-ten-kingdoms.e: In 937 [[e:li-bian|Xu Zhigao]] made [[e:yang-pu|Yang Pu]] abdicate and founded his own dynasty, soon renamed [[s:later-tang|Tang]] and known as [[s:southern-tang|Southern Tang]], taking the name Li Bian. The Yang family was kept in confinement and later massacred.

wu-zhou.t: The Zhou dynasty proclaimed by Wu Zetian, the only woman in Chinese history to rule as emperor in her own name, interrupting the Tang from 690 to 705.
wu-zhou.o: [[e:wu-zetian|Wu Zhao]], a concubine of [[e:emperor-taizong-of-tang|Emperor Taizong]], became empress to [[e:emperor-gaozong-of-tang|Emperor Gaozong]] in 655 and gradually took over government as he fell ill. After his death in 683 she deposed her son [[e:emperor-zhongzong-of-tang|Zhongzong]], kept [[e:emperor-ruizong-of-tang|Ruizong]] as a figurehead, crushed a [[s:later-tang|Tang]] princes' revolt and in 690 proclaimed her own [[s:western-zhou|Zhou dynasty]], with [[e:luoyang|Luoyang]], renamed Shendu, as capital.
wu-zhou.r: [[e:wu-zetian|Wu Zetian]] promoted [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]], using the [[e:great-cloud-sutra|Great Cloud Sutra]] to support a female ruler, and favoured the [[e:maitreya|Maitreya]] cult. She widened the [[e:imperial-examination|examination system]] to recruit men from outside the old north-western aristocracy, invented new written characters and relied on informers and secret police such as [[e:lai-junchen|Lai Junchen]]. The frontier wars against the [[s:second-turkic-khaganate|Second Turkic Khaganate]], Khitan and [[e:tibetans|Tibetans]] had mixed results.
wu-zhou.e: In 705 ministers led by [[e:zhang-jianzhi|Zhang Jianzhi]] killed her favourites, the Zhang brothers, and forced the aged [[e:wu-zetian|Wu Zetian]] to abdicate in favour of [[e:emperor-zhongzong-of-tang|Zhongzong]], restoring the [[s:tang-dynasty|Tang Dynasty]]. She died later that year and was buried with [[e:emperor-gaozong-of-tang|Gaozong]] at the [[e:qianling-mausoleum|Qianling mausoleum]].

western-shu.t: A brief breakaway state in Sichuan, ruled by Qiao Zong after a mutiny of 405, which the Eastern Jin reconquered in 413.
western-shu.o: In 405 [[s:eastern-jin|Eastern Jin]] troops in [[e:sichuan|Sichuan]], unwilling to campaign against [[e:huan-xuan|Huan Xuan's]] surviving relatives, mutinied and killed their commander Mao Qu. They chose the officer [[e:qiao-zong|Qiao Zong]] as leader, and he proclaimed himself Prince of [[e:chengdu|Chengdu]].
western-shu.r: Western Shu held the [[e:chengdu|Chengdu]] plain and sought protection by accepting the overlordship of [[s:later-qin|Later Qin]], which recognised [[e:qiao-zong|Qiao Zong]] as King of Shu. It also sheltered Huan clan fugitives and joined attacks on [[s:eastern-jin|Eastern Jin]] territory along the [[e:yangtze-river|Yangtze]].
western-shu.e: In 412 [[e:emperor-wu-of-liu-song|Liu Yu]] sent [[e:zhu-lingshi|Zhu Lingshi]], who advanced by an unexpected route and captured [[e:chengdu|Chengdu]] in 413. [[e:qiao-zong|Qiao Zong]] fled and hanged himself, and [[e:sichuan|Sichuan]] returned to the [[s:eastern-jin|Eastern Jin]].

warmians.t: Prussian people of Warmia, around the Vistula Lagoon, whose land became the Prince-Bishopric of Warmia after the Teutonic conquest.
warmians.o: The Warmians lived in [[s:prince-bishopric-of-warmia|Warmia]], south-east of the [[e:vistula-lagoon|Vistula Lagoon]] in today's northern [[e:poland|Poland]]. They were one of the Prussian peoples recorded by [[e:peter-of-dusburg|Peter of Dusburg]], with settlements along the [[e:pasleka|Pasłęka]] and [[e:lyna|Łyna]] rivers.
warmians.r: Warmian society was led by nobles who held hillforts and controlled farming land, and its people kept the Prussian religion. The coast linked them to Baltic trade, including amber.
warmians.e: The [[e:teutonic-order|Teutonic Order]] invaded in 1239, founding [[e:balga-castle|Balga]] castle, and soon dominated [[s:prince-bishopric-of-warmia|Warmia]]. During the [[e:great-prussian-uprising|Great Prussian Uprising]] the Warmians fought under their leader [[e:glappe|Glappe]], who was captured and hanged at [[e:konigsberg|Königsberg]]. By 1274 they were subdued, and their land became the Bishopric of Warmia, a prince-bishopric that passed to [[e:poland|Poland]] in 1466.

western-confederacy.t: An alliance of Native nations of the Great Lakes and Ohio country that resisted American expansion and inflicted the worst defeat ever suffered by the US Army against Native forces.
western-confederacy.o: The [[e:treaty-of-paris-1783|Treaty of Paris]] of 1783 gave the [[s:united-states|United States]] land north of the [[e:ohio-river|Ohio River]] that its Native inhabitants had never ceded. Building on earlier alliances, [[e:shawnee|Shawnee]], [[e:miami-people|Miami]], [[e:lenape|Lenape]], [[e:wyandot|Wyandot]], [[e:odawa|Odawa]], [[e:ojibwe|Ojibwe]], [[e:potawatomi|Potawatomi]] and others coordinated through councils, with support from the [[s:mohawk-nation|Mohawk]] leader [[e:joseph-brant|Joseph Brant]], insisting on the [[e:ohio|Ohio]] as the boundary.
western-confederacy.r: The confederacy was a loose alliance of autonomous nations rather than a government, meeting in council and relying on war leaders such as [[e:little-turtle|Little Turtle]] of the [[e:miami-people|Miami]] and [[e:blue-jacket|Blue Jacket]] of the [[e:shawnee|Shawnee]]. British posts at [[e:detroit|Detroit]] and elsewhere supplied arms. It defeated [[e:josiah-harmar|Josiah Harmar]] in 1790 and destroyed [[e:arthur-st-clair|Arthur St. Clair's]] army on the [[e:wabash-river|Wabash]] in 1791.
western-confederacy.e: General [[e:anthony-wayne|Anthony Wayne]] defeated the alliance at Fallen [[e:timber|Timbers]] in 1794, and the British refused shelter at [[e:fort-miamis|Fort Miami]]. The [[e:treaty-of-greenville|Treaty of Greenville]] in 1795 ceded most of present-day [[e:ohio|Ohio]]. Resistance revived later in [[s:tecumsehs-confederacy|Tecumseh's Confederacy]].

wambu-kingdom.t: An Ovimbundu kingdom of the central Angolan highlands whose lands became the site of the colonial city of Huambo.
wambu-kingdom.o: Wambu (Huambo) was one of the [[e:ovimbundu|Ovimbundu]] kingdoms that emerged on the [[e:benguela|Benguela]] highlands by the 18th century, alongside the [[s:bailundo-kingdom|Bailundo Kingdom]] and the [[s:viye-kingdom|Viye Kingdom]]. Like its neighbours, it grew as a fortified raiding state with ruling lineages of mixed local and immigrant origin.
wambu-kingdom.r: Its kings ruled from hilltop fortresses through titled officials and village heads. Wambu's people farmed [[e:maize|maize]] and beans and joined [[e:ovimbundu|Ovimbundu]] long-distance caravans carrying slaves, [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]], beeswax and later [[e:rubber|rubber]] between the interior and [[e:benguela|Benguela]]. Detailed records of its rulers are scarce.
wambu-kingdom.e: Wambu was drawn into the [[s:bailundo-kingdom|Bailundo]] revolt of 1902 and occupied by Portuguese forces by 1902–03. In 1912 the Portuguese founded the city of Huambo on its lands, which became one of [[e:angola|Angola's]] main cities.

wattasid-sultanate.t: The family of Marinid viziers who became sultans of Fez, ruling a shrunken Morocco squeezed between Portuguese enclaves and the rising Saadis.
wattasid-sultanate.o: The Banu Wattas, [[e:zanata-berbers|Zenata]] kin of the [[s:marinid-sultanate|Marinids]], governed [[s:kingdom-of-morocco|Morocco]] as regents and [[e:vizier|viziers]] from 1420. After the last [[e:marinid-dynasty|Marinid]] sultan was killed in [[e:fez|Fez]] in 1465, a sharif ruled the city until [[e:muhammad-al-shaykh-al-wattasi|Muhammad al-Shaykh al-Wattasi]], who had just lost [[e:asilah|Arzila]] to Portugal in 1471, captured Fez in 1472 and proclaimed himself sultan.
wattasid-sultanate.r: Wattasid authority rarely reached far beyond [[e:fez|Fez]] and the north. The [[s:hintata-emirate|Hintata emirate]] held [[e:marrakesh|Marrakesh]], local lords ruled [[e:chefchaouen|Chefchaouen]] and [[e:tetouan|Tetouan]], and the [[s:kingdom-of-portugal|Kingdom of Portugal]] seized much of the Atlantic coast. The dynasty relied on truces with Portugal and the prestige of Fez's scholars, while [[e:sufism|Sufi]] brotherhoods led resistance to the Christians.
wattasid-sultanate.e: The [[s:saadi-sultanate|Saadi Sultanate]], leading holy war from the south, defeated the Wattasids and took [[e:fez|Fez]] in 1549. [[e:ali-abu-hassun|Ali Abu Hassun]] briefly retook the city in 1554 with Ottoman help from the [[s:regency-of-algiers|Regency of Algiers]], but was killed the same year, ending the dynasty.

wuhuan.t: Nomads of the north-eastern frontier who served the Han as border guards and cavalry until Cao Cao crushed them at White Wolf Mountain in 207.
wuhuan.o: Like the [[s:xianbei|Xianbei]], the Wuhuan were survivors of the [[s:donghu|Donghu]], who took refuge at the Wuhuan mountains after [[e:modu-chanyu|Modu]] of the [[e:xiongnu-empire|Xiongnu]] destroyed them around 206 BCE. They lived in eastern [[e:inner-mongolia|Inner Mongolia]] and western [[e:liaoning|Liaoning]] and paid tribute to the Xiongnu.
wuhuan.r: After the Han general [[e:huo-qubing|Huo Qubing]] defeated the [[e:xiongnu-empire|Xiongnu]] in 119 BCE, the [[s:han-dynasty|Han Dynasty]] resettled Wuhuan bands along its frontier [[e:commandery|commanderies]] as guards and set up a Protector of the Wuhuan. They were herders and hunters ruled by elected chiefs, without a single king, and Wuhuan cavalry became famous [[e:mercenary|mercenaries]] in Han wars.
wuhuan.e: In the late 2nd century Wuhuan chiefs such as [[e:tadun|Tadun]] allied with the warlord [[e:yuan-shao|Yuan Shao]]. In 207 [[e:cao-cao|Cao Cao]] crossed the mountains and killed Tadun at [[e:battle-of-white-wolf-mountain|White Wolf Mountain]], then moved the Wuhuan into [[e:china|China]], where their horsemen served his armies and they gradually merged with the Chinese and the [[s:xianbei|Xianbei]].

western-zhou.t: The dynasty that overthrew the Shang, introduced the idea of the Mandate of Heaven and ruled northern China through kinsmen planted across the land.
western-zhou.o: The Zhou were a people of the [[e:wei-river|Wei River]] valley in [[e:shaanxi|Shaanxi]] who grew strong under [[e:king-wen-of-zhou|King Wen]]. His son [[e:king-wu-of-zhou|King Wu]] defeated the last [[s:shang-dynasty|Shang]] king, [[e:di-xin|Di Xin]], at [[e:battle-of-muye|Muye]] in 1046 BCE. After Wu's early death the [[e:duke-of-zhou|Duke of Zhou]] acted as regent for the young [[e:king-cheng-of-zhou|King Cheng]], crushed a rebellion of Shang loyalists and royal brothers, and built an eastern capital at [[e:luoyang|Luoyi]].
western-zhou.r: The kings ruled from [[e:haojing|Haojing]] and [[e:fengjing|Fengjing]] near modern Xi'an and justified their power as the [[e:mandate-of-heaven|Mandate of Heaven]], given to virtuous rulers and withdrawn from wicked ones. They granted lands to relatives and allies, who founded states such as the [[s:state-of-lu|State of Lu]], the [[s:state-of-jin|State of Jin]] and the [[s:state-of-yan|State of Yan]]. Long bronze inscriptions record appointments, gifts and lawsuits. In 841 BCE a revolt in the capital drove out King Li, the first exactly dated year in Chinese history.
western-zhou.e: In 771 BCE the Marquis of Shen and the [[e:quanrong|Quanrong]] sacked [[e:haojing|Haojing]] and killed [[e:king-you-of-zhou|King You]]. [[e:king-ping-of-zhou|King Ping]] re-established the court at [[e:luoyang|Luoyang]], beginning the [[s:eastern-zhou|Eastern Zhou]]. Later [[e:confucianism|Confucians]] idealised the early Western Zhou as [[e:china|China's]] golden age of ritual order.
western-zhou.re: Zhou ancestral religion and worship of Heaven

warri-kingdom.t: Itsekiri kingdom of the western Niger delta, founded by a Benin prince, whose kings adopted Catholicism and traded with Europe from the 16th century.
warri-kingdom.o: Itsekiri tradition holds that [[e:ginuwa|Ginuwa]], a prince of the [[s:benin-empire|Benin Empire]], left [[e:benin-empire|Benin]] around 1480 with followers and settled among the creeks of the western delta. His descendants took the title [[e:olu-of-warri|Olu]], and the capital was established at [[e:ode-itsekiri|Ode-Itsekiri]], known to Europeans as Big Warri.
warri-kingdom.r: Warri's kings controlled trade between the interior and European ships. Portuguese missionaries converted the court, and around 1600 [[e:dom-domingos-of-warri|Olu Dom Domingos]], educated in Portugal, married a Portuguese woman. Warri dealt in slaves, cloth and later [[e:palm-oil|palm oil]]. After the death of [[e:akengbuwa|Olu Akengbuwa]] in 1848, rival houses could not agree on a successor and governors of the river held power.
warri-kingdom.e: The British signed a protection treaty in 1884 and in 1894 destroyed [[e:ebrohimi|Ebrohimi]], the town of the governor [[e:nana-olomu|Nana Olomu]]. Warri became part of the [[s:niger-coast-protectorate|Niger Coast Protectorate]]. The kingship was restored in 1936, and the [[e:olu-of-warri|Olu of Warri]] still reigns.

west-ukrainian-peoples-republic.t: The Ukrainian state of eastern Galicia, proclaimed in Lviv in 1918, which fought Poland and briefly united with the Ukrainian People's Republic.
west-ukrainian-peoples-republic.o: As the [[s:austro-hungarian-empire|Austro-Hungarian Empire]] collapsed, Ukrainian soldiers seized [[e:lviv|Lviv]] on 1 November 1918, and a Ukrainian National Council proclaimed the West [[s:ukrainian-peoples-republic|Ukrainian People's Republic]] over eastern [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria|Galicia]], northern [[s:duchy-of-bukovina|Bukovina]] and [[e:carpathian-ruthenia|Transcarpathia]]. [[e:yevhen-petrushevych|Yevhen Petrushevych]] became its president and [[e:kost-levytsky|Kost Levytsky]] headed the government.
west-ukrainian-peoples-republic.r: The republic quickly built a working administration, police and courts out of former Austrian institutions and formed the disciplined Ukrainian Galician Army. Polish residents of [[e:lviv|Lviv]] resisted, and the [[e:polish-ukrainian-war|Polish-Ukrainian War]] began; the [[e:ukrainians|Ukrainians]] lost Lviv in November and moved the capital to [[e:ternopil|Ternopil]] and then [[e:ivano-frankivsk|Stanislaviv]]. In January 1919 the republic proclaimed union with the [[s:ukrainian-peoples-republic|Ukrainian People's Republic]], keeping its own government.
west-ukrainian-peoples-republic.e: A Polish offensive in mid 1919 drove the Galician Army across the [[e:zbruch-river|Zbruch]] in July, and the [[s:second-polish-republic|Second Polish Republic]] occupied the whole territory. [[e:yevhen-petrushevych|Petrushevych]]'s government went into exile, and the [[e:allies|Allies]] recognised Polish rule over eastern [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria|Galicia]] in 1923.

western-xia.t: The empire of the Tangut people in north-west China, with its own script and Buddhist culture, destroyed by Genghis Khan in 1227.
western-xia.o: The [[e:tanguts|Tanguts]] were a [[e:tibeto-burman-languages|Tibeto-Burman]] people whose [[e:tuoba|Tuoba]] chiefs governed the Xiazhou region in the [[e:ordos-plateau|Ordos]] as [[s:later-tang|Tang]] and [[e:song-dynasty|Song]] governors. [[e:li-jiqian|Li Jiqian]] broke with the Song in 982, his son [[e:li-deming|Li Deming]] expanded west into the [[e:gansu-corridor|Hexi Corridor]], and in 1038 [[e:li-yuanhao|Li Yuanhao]] proclaimed himself emperor of [[s:ming-xia|Great Xia]], with his capital at [[e:yinchuan|Xingqing]] (modern Yinchuan).
western-xia.r: Western Xia combined a tribal military aristocracy with Chinese-style ministries. [[e:li-yuanhao|Li Yuanhao]] introduced a distinctive [[e:tanguts|Tangut]] script in 1036, used for laws, histories and a huge translation of the Buddhist canon. The state controlled trade routes between [[e:china|China]] and [[e:central-asia|Central Asia]] and fought the [[s:song-dynasty|Song Dynasty]], the [[s:liao-dynasty|Liao dynasty]] and the [[s:jin-dynasty-1115-1234|Jin dynasty]] (1115-1234), extracting [[e:subsidy|subsidies]] from [[e:song-dynasty|Song]] after 1044.
western-xia.e: The [[e:mongols|Mongols]] attacked from 1205. After Western Xia refused to join the campaign against the [[s:khwarazmian-empire|Khwarazmian Empire]], [[e:genghis-khan|Genghis Khan]] invaded in 1226; he died during the siege in 1227, and the capital fell soon after. The [[e:tanguts|Tangut]] population was massacred or scattered.

witbooi-nama.t: The Nama community of Gibeon led by Hendrik Witbooi, the most persistent opponent of German colonial rule in Namibia.
witbooi-nama.o: The Witboois, or Khowesin, were an [[e:oorlam|Oorlam]] group from the northern Cape. Around 1863 [[e:kido-witbooi|Kido Witbooi]] led them north from [[s:pella|Pella]] to [[e:gibeon-namibia|Gibeon]] in central southern [[e:namibia|Namibia]], where a Rhenish mission was established and they became one of the leading [[e:nama-people|Nama]] communities.
witbooi-nama.r: [[e:hendrik-witbooi|Hendrik Witbooi]], grandson of [[e:kido-witbooi|Kido]], saw himself as a Christian leader with a divine mission and fought long campaigns against the [[e:herero-people|Herero]] for [[e:cattle|cattle]] and land. Literate and politically shrewd, he kept letters and a diary that are major sources. He refused German protection until a surprise German attack on his base at [[e:hornkranz|Hornkranz]] in 1893 forced him to submit in 1894.
witbooi-nama.e: [[e:hendrik-witbooi|Witbooi]] fought as a German ally for ten years, then rose against [[s:german-south-west-africa|German South West Africa]] in October 1904. He was killed in 1905, and the Witbooi were deported, many dying on [[e:shark-island-concentration-camp|Shark Island]]; his image appears on Namibian banknotes.

wav-state.t: A small Chauhan Rajput state on the border of the Rann of Kutch in northern Gujarat, ruled by a Rana.
wav-state.o: Wav, or Vav, was held by [[e:chauhan|Chauhan Rajputs]] who claimed descent from the medieval Chauhan rulers of [[e:rajasthan|Rajasthan]]. The register dates the state to around 1700. It lay in the desert fringe where [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] meets the [[e:rann-of-kutch|Rann]] and [[e:sind|Sind]].
wav-state.r: The Rana ruled a dry territory of grazing land and [[e:millet|millet]] fields. In the British period Wav was a minor state under the [[s:palanpur-state|Palanpur]] and later the [[e:banas-kantha-agency|Banas Kantha Agency]]. Few further details are widely recorded.
wav-state.e: Wav merged into [[s:bombay-presidency|Bombay Province]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960, in [[e:banaskantha-district|Banaskantha district]].

western-wei.t: The western half of the divided Northern Wei, controlled by Yuwen Tai, whose militia system and Guanlong elite laid the foundations of the Sui and Tang.
western-wei.o: [[e:yuwen-tai|Yuwen Tai]], a general of [[s:xianbei|Xianbei]] descent, controlled the [[e:guanzhong|Guanzhong]] region around [[e:changan|Chang'an]]. When the [[s:northern-wei|Northern Wei]] emperor [[e:emperor-xiaowu-of-northern-wei|Xiaowu]] fled to him in 534, [[s:yuwen-xianbei|Yuwen]] Tai received him, then had him poisoned and in 535 installed [[e:emperor-wen-of-western-wei|Yuan Baoju]] as Emperor Wen of [[s:western-wei-206-bc|Western Wei]].
western-wei.r: [[s:western-wei-206-bc|Western Wei]] was poorer and smaller than [[s:eastern-wei|Eastern Wei]], so [[e:yuwen-tai|Yuwen Tai]] built a new system. With the minister [[e:su-chuo|Su Chuo]] he issued administrative reforms, revived offices modelled on the [[e:rites-of-zhou|Rites of Zhou]] and created the [[e:fubing-system|fubing]] militia, enrolling Chinese and [[s:xianbei|Xianbei]] soldiers under Eight Pillars of State. This forged the [[e:guanlong-aristocracy|Guanlong aristocracy]]. Western Wei took [[e:sichuan|Sichuan]] in 553 and sacked the [[s:liang-dynasty|Liang dynasty]]'s capital [[e:jiangling|Jiangling]] in 554.
western-wei.e: [[e:yuwen-tai|Yuwen Tai]] died in 556, and in 557 his nephew [[e:yuwen-hu|Yuwen Hu]] had the last emperor abdicate to [[s:yuwen-xianbei|Yuwen]] Tai's son [[e:yuwen-jue|Yuwen Jue]], founding the [[s:northern-zhou|Northern Zhou]]. The [[s:sui-dynasty|Sui Dynasty]] and [[s:tang-dynasty|Tang Dynasty]] founders came from Western Wei's [[e:guanlong-aristocracy|Guanlong]] elite.

western-kara-khanid-khanate.t: The western branch of the Kara-Khanid dynasty, ruling Samarkand and Bukhara under Seljuk and then Qara Khitai overlordship.
western-kara-khanid-khanate.o: When the [[s:kara-khanid-khanate|Kara-Khanid Khanate]] divided around 1042, [[e:ibrahim-tamghach-khan|Ibrahim Tamghach Khan]], son of [[e:nasr-ibn-ali|Nasr ibn Ali]], took [[e:transoxiana|Transoxiana]] and made [[e:samarkand|Samarkand]] his capital, building a strong, centralised state that his descendants ruled.
western-kara-khanid-khanate.r: [[e:ibrahim-tamghach-khan|Ibrahim Tamghach Khan]] was remembered for justice, founding hospitals and [[e:madrasa|madrasas]] in [[e:samarkand|Samarkand]]. The khans ruled a settled Persian-speaking population with Turkic troops, and [[e:bukhara|Bukhara]] was governed in time by the hereditary Burhan family of religious leaders. In 1089 the Seljuk sultan [[e:malik-shah-i|Malik-Shah]] took Samarkand, making the khans [[e:vassal|vassals]].
western-kara-khanid-khanate.e: After the [[s:qara-khitai|Qara Khitai]] crushed the Seljuk sultan [[e:ahmad-sanjar|Ahmad Sanjar]] at the Qatwan steppe in 1141, the khans became [[e:qara-khitai|Qara Khitai]] [[e:vassal|vassals]]. The last khan, Uthman, was executed in 1212 by [[e:ala-ad-din-muhammad-ii|Muhammad II]] of the [[s:khwarazmian-empire|Khwarazmian Empire]] after a revolt in [[e:samarkand|Samarkand]].

wankaner-state.t: A Jhala Rajput state of Kathiawar on the Machhu river, known for its palaces and for rulers prominent in Indian public life.
wankaner-state.o: Wankaner was founded in 1605 by Sartanji, a member of the [[e:jhala|Jhala]] ruling house of [[e:halvad|Halvad]] (later [[s:dhrangadhra-state|Dhrangadhra State]]), who took lands on the [[e:machchhu-river|Machhu]] river in northern [[e:kathiawar|Kathiawar]].
wankaner-state.r: The [[e:british-raj|Raj]] Sahebs ruled a territory of [[e:cotton|cotton]] and grain villages, paying tribute to the [[e:gaekwads|Gaekwads]] and [[s:junagadh-state|Junagadh]] before British protection after 1807. [[e:amarsinhji-of-wankaner|Amarsinhji]], who reigned from 1881 to 1948, built the [[e:ranjit-vilas-palace|Ranjit Vilas Palace]] and modernised the administration. It was an eleven-gun salute state.
wankaner-state.e: Wankaner merged into the [[s:saurashtra-state|United State of Saurashtra]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960. Its royal family remained active in politics, and [[e:digvijaysinhji|Digvijaysinhji]] served as a Union minister.

wahidi-sultanate.t: A coastal sultanate of the Wahidi tribe, centred on Balhaf, near the site of the ancient incense port of Qana.
wahidi-sultanate.o: The Wahidi tribe held the coast and hinterland between the Aulaqi lands and [[s:kingdom-of-hadramawt|Hadramawt]]. The territory was divided among several branches, and the sultanate based at [[e:balhaf|Balhaf]] emerged as a separate ruling line by around 1830.
wahidi-sultanate.r: The sultans ruled a coastal strip and valleys inland, living from fishing, farming and trade. Near Bir Ali in their territory lay the ruins of [[e:qana-yemen|Qana]], the main port of the ancient [[s:kingdom-of-hadramawt|Kingdom of Hadramawt]]. The Wahidi sultanates signed treaties with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] in the late 19th century and formed part of the [[s:aden-protectorate|Aden Protectorate]]. [[e:balhaf|Balhaf]] joined the [[s:federation-of-south-arabia|Federation of South Arabia]] in the early 1960s.
wahidi-sultanate.e: In 1967 the [[e:national-liberation-front-south-yemen|National Liberation Front]] took over the region and the sultanate was abolished and incorporated into [[s:south-yemen|South Yemen]].

wadhwan-state.t: A Jhala Rajput state of Kathiawar on the Bhogavo river, one of the branches of the Halvad ruling house.
wadhwan-state.o: Wadhwan was founded in 1630 by a cadet of the [[e:jhala|Jhala]] house of [[e:halvad|Halvad]], the line of [[s:dhrangadhra-state|Dhrangadhra State]]. The town had an older history as a medieval fortified centre.
wadhwan-state.r: The Thakore Sahibs ruled a territory of [[e:cotton|cotton]] villages, paying tribute to the [[e:gaekwads|Gaekwads]] before British protection after 1807. A British civil station grew up beside the town, later Surendranagar, and the railway made the area a cotton market. It was a nine-gun salute state.
wadhwan-state.e: Wadhwan merged into the [[s:saurashtra-state|United State of Saurashtra]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960. Its old town is now part of Surendranagar.

western-qin.t: A Qifu Xianbei kingdom in Gansu that rose from the Former Qin collapse and survived among stronger neighbours for nearly half a century.
western-qin.o: The [[e:qifu-clan|Qifu]] were a [[s:xianbei|Xianbei]] clan settled around the upper [[e:yellow-river|Yellow River]] in [[e:gansu|Gansu]]. After [[s:former-qin|Former Qin]]'s collapse, [[e:qifu-guoren|Qifu Guoren]] declared himself ruler in 385, with his capital at Yuanchuan near modern [[e:zhongyong-of-wu|Yuzhong]].
western-qin.r: [[s:qin-xue-ju|Western Qin]] was a small state of [[s:xianbei|Xianbei]] herders and Chinese farmers, governed by tribal chiefs alongside Chinese officials. [[e:qifu-gangui|Qifu Gangui]] briefly submitted to [[s:later-qin|Later Qin]] from 400 to 409 before restoring the state, which then conquered [[s:southern-liang|Southern Liang]] in 414. [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] flourished: an inscription of 420 in the [[e:bingling-temple|Bingling Temple]] caves near the later capital Fuhan is the oldest dated one in a Chinese cave temple.
western-qin.e: Under attack from [[s:northern-liang|Northern Liang]] and [[s:helian-xia|Helian Xia]], the last ruler, [[e:qifu-mumo|Qifu Mumo]], tried to flee to [[s:northern-wei|Northern Wei]] but was captured by Helian Xia, which killed him and his clan in 431.

wehali.t: The ritual centre of central Timor, whose ruler was honoured as the source of authority by many Tetun and Bunak domains.
wehali.o: Wewiku-Wehali lay on the south coast of central [[e:timor|Timor]], in today's [[s:malaka|Malaka]] Regency. Its traditions place it at the origin of the land, the first dry ground to emerge from the sea. The register's start of 1500 reflects its appearance in Portuguese records of the 16th century, when sandalwood traders reached Timor.
wehali.r: Wehali was ruled by a sacred figure who remained still and inactive, while executive rulers called liurai governed and dealt with outsiders. Many domains across [[e:timor|Timor]] acknowledged Wehali as their ritual elder. Society was matrilineal. Sandalwood and beeswax were traded to Portuguese, Chinese and [[s:gowa-sultanate|Makassar]] merchants.
wehali.e: The Portuguese attacked Wehali in 1642, weakening its influence. Divided between Portuguese and [[e:dutch|Dutch]] spheres, its domains were brought under direct Dutch control by 1906. Wehali remains an important ritual centre in Indonesian [[e:west-timor|West Timor]].

wassa.t: An Akan kingdom on the goldfields of south-western Ghana, long squeezed between Denkyira, the Ashanti Empire and European forts on the coast.
wassa.o: Wassa emerged in the 17th century in the forest between the [[e:pra-river|Pra]] and [[e:ankobra-river|Ankobra]] rivers, a region rich in alluvial gold around [[e:tarkwa|Tarkwa]]. It was for a time subject to [[s:denkyira|Denkyira]], and after the collapse of [[e:denkyira|Denkyira]] in 1701 it passed under the influence of the [[s:ashanti-empire|Ashanti Empire]]. The state later divided into two branches, Wassa Fiase and Wassa Amenfi.
wassa.r: Each branch was ruled by a king chosen from a royal matrilineage and advised by chiefs and elders, in the common [[e:akan|Akan]] pattern. Gold mining and trading supplied the coastal forts of the [[s:dutch-gold-coast|Dutch Gold Coast]] and the British, and control of the paths to the sea gave Wassa some leverage. It repeatedly allied with the [[e:fante|Fante]] and the British against [[e:ashanti-empire|Ashanti]] claims to the coast.
wassa.e: After the British victory over [[e:ashanti-empire|Ashanti]] in 1874, Wassa was absorbed into the new [[s:gold-coast-colony|Gold Coast Colony]]. Its goldfields became the centre of the colonial mining industry from the 1870s, and the Wassa traditional areas survive within modern Ghana.

western-jin.t: The Sima family's dynasty that reunited China in 280 after the Three Kingdoms, only to tear itself apart in the War of the Eight Princes and lose the north.
western-jin.o: After decades in which the Sima family dominated [[s:cao-wei|Cao Wei]], [[e:emperor-wu-of-jin|Sima Yan]] forced the last Wei emperor to abdicate in 266 and founded the [[s:jin-dynasty-1115-1234|Jin dynasty]], ruling from [[e:luoyang|Luoyang]] as [[e:emperor-wu-of-han|Emperor Wu]]. [[s:shu-han|Shu Han]] was already conquered, and in 280 Jin forces took [[s:eastern-wu|Eastern Wu]], reuniting [[e:china|China]].
western-jin.r: [[e:emperor-wu-of-han|Emperor Wu]] gave imperial princes their own armies and fiefs, demobilised provincial forces and introduced land allotment rules. The court and great families were famous for extravagance, and the Pure Conversation pioneered under Wei by the [[e:seven-sages-of-the-bamboo-grove|Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove]] flourished. Under Emperor Hui, who was mentally incapable, Empress Jia's intrigues triggered the [[e:war-of-the-eight-princes|War of the Eight Princes]] from 291 to 306.
western-jin.e: Exhausted by civil war, the dynasty could not resist risings by peoples settled inside the frontier. [[s:han-zhao|Han Zhao]] armies sacked [[e:luoyang|Luoyang]] in 311 and took [[e:changan|Chang'an]] in 316, capturing Emperor Min. A branch of the Sima family continued the dynasty in the south as the [[s:eastern-jin|Eastern Jin]].

wampanoag-confederacy.t: The alliance of Algonquian communities in south-eastern New England whose sachem Massasoit befriended the Plymouth Pilgrims and whose son Metacom led King Philip's War.
wampanoag-confederacy.o: The Wampanoag, People of the First Light, lived in some 60 or more communities across south-eastern [[s:province-of-massachusetts-bay|Massachusetts]], eastern [[s:rhode|Rhode]] Island, [[e:cape-cod|Cape Cod]], [[e:marthas-vineyard|Martha's Vineyard]] and [[e:nantucket|Nantucket]]. A devastating epidemic in 1616 to 1619 killed a large share of them shortly before the Pilgrims arrived, and the sachem [[e:massasoit|Massasoit]], ruling from [[e:sowams|Sowams]], held the communities together.
wampanoag-confederacy.r: Local sachems governed their own villages but owed loyalty to the paramount sachem, who could call councils and warriors. People farmed [[e:maize|maize]] and fished seasonally along the coast. In 1621 [[e:massasoit|Massasoit]] made an alliance with [[s:plymouth-colony|Plymouth Colony]], aided by the interpreter [[e:tisquantum|Tisquantum]], and shared the harvest feast later called the first Thanksgiving. Missionaries such as [[e:john-eliot-missionary|John Eliot]] founded praying towns, and the Bible was printed in Wampanoag in 1663.
wampanoag-confederacy.e: English land hunger and pressure on [[e:massasoit|Massasoit's]] sons [[e:wamsutta|Wamsutta]] and [[e:metacom|Metacom]] led to [[e:king-philips-war|King Philip's War]] in 1675. Metacom was killed in 1676 and many captives were sold into [[e:slavery|slavery]]. The [[e:mashpee-wampanoag-tribe|Mashpee]] and [[e:wampanoag-tribe-of-gay-head-aquinnah|Aquinnah Wampanoag]] survive.

western-liang.t: A Chinese-ruled kingdom at Dunhuang, the westernmost of the Sixteen Kingdoms, whose founder Li Gao was later claimed as an ancestor by the Tang emperors.
western-liang.o: [[e:li-gao|Li Gao]], a Chinese official of the [[e:li-clan-of-longxi|Longxi Li]] family, governed [[e:dunhuang|Dunhuang]] under [[s:northern-liang|Northern Liang]]. In 400 local officials proclaimed him Duke of [[s:liang-liang-shidu|Liang]], and he broke away to rule the western [[e:gansu-corridor|Hexi Corridor]], moving his capital from Dunhuang to [[e:jiuquan|Jiuquan]] in 405.
western-liang.r: [[e:li-gao|Li Gao]] governed in the Confucian manner, encouraging schools, farming and irrigation, and acknowledged the [[s:eastern-jin|Eastern Jin]] as his sovereign. [[e:dunhuang|Dunhuang]], at the junction of the [[e:silk-road|Silk Roads]], was a centre of trade and Buddhist activity, and [[s:western-liang-555-587|Western Liang]] preserved Chinese learning on the far frontier.
western-liang.e: [[e:li-gao|Li Gao's]] son [[e:li-xin-western-liang|Li Xin]] was killed in battle with [[s:northern-liang|Northern Liang]] in 420; [[e:juqu-mengxun|Juqu Mengxun]] then took [[e:jiuquan|Jiuquan]], and in 421 he flooded [[e:dunhuang|Dunhuang]] and killed [[e:li-xun-western-liang|Li Xun]]. The [[e:tang-dynasty|Tang Dynasty's]] Li emperors traced their ancestry to Li [[e:gao|Gao]].

western-turkic-khaganate.t: The western half of the Turkic empire, which ruled the steppe from the Altai to the Volga and the oasis cities of Sogdiana and the Tarim.
western-turkic-khaganate.o: The [[e:first-turkic-khaganate|First Turkic Khaganate]], founded in 552 by [[e:bumin-qaghan|Bumin]], gave its western lands to his brother [[e:istami|Istämi]], who with [[e:persia|Persia]] destroyed the [[s:hephthalite-empire|Hephthalite Empire]]. Rivalries within the ruling [[e:ashina-clan|Ashina clan]] led to a formal split around 603, when [[e:tardu-shad|Tardu]]'s successors ruled the west independently of the [[s:eastern-turkic-khaganate|Eastern Turkic Khaganate]].
western-turkic-khaganate.r: The [[e:khagan|khagans]] ruled from summer pastures and courts such as [[e:suyab|Suyab]] in the Chu valley over the 'On Oq', ten arrows or tribes in two wings. Sogdian merchants and scribes served them, and they sent embassies to [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]], allying with [[e:heraclius|Heraclius]] against [[e:persia|Persia]] in 627. Under [[e:tong-yabghu-khagan|Tong Yabghu]], whom [[e:xuanzang|Xuanzang]] met near Suyab around 628 to 630, the khaganate reached its height, collecting tribute from Sogdian cities and [[e:tokharistan|Tokharistan]].
western-turkic-khaganate.e: After [[e:tong-yabghu-khagan|Tong Yabghu]]'s murder, civil wars divided the tribes, and in 657 the [[s:later-tang|Tang]] general [[e:su-dingfang|Su Dingfang]] defeated the [[e:khagan|khagan]] [[e:ashina-helu|Ashina Helu]]. The [[e:ashina-clan|Ashina]] were installed as Tang puppets until about 742; power passed to the [[s:turgesh-khaganate|Turgesh Khaganate]] and the [[s:karluk-yabgu|Karluk Yabgu]].

witu-sultanate.t: A refuge state founded on the Kenyan mainland by the deposed rulers of Pate, briefly a German protectorate before passing to Britain.
witu-sultanate.o: In 1858 [[e:ahmad-simba|Ahmad ibn Fumo Bakari]], called Simba, a member of the Nabhani family that had ruled the [[s:pate-sultanate|Pate Sultanate]], fled from the [[s:sultanate-of-zanzibar|Sultanate of Zanzibar]]'s forces to the forests of the mainland and founded a new sultanate at [[e:witu|Witu]], north-west of [[s:lamu|Lamu]]. It drew runaway slaves and opponents of Zanzibar.
witu-sultanate.r: [[e:witu|Witu]] was a small, fortified state of farmers and former slaves, ruled by the Nabhani sultan with [[e:swahili|Swahili]] notables. To protect himself from [[s:sultanate-of-zanzibar|Zanzibar]], [[e:ahmad-simba|Ahmad Simba]] accepted a German [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] in 1885, negotiated by the [[e:denhardt-brothers|Denhardt brothers]], and the area was known as German Witu or Wituland.
witu-sultanate.e: Under the [[e:heligoland-zanzibar-treaty|Heligoland-Zanzibar Treaty]] of 1890 [[e:germany|Germany]] handed [[e:witu|Witu]] to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]]. After Germans were killed there, a British force sacked the town in 1890 and [[e:sultan|Sultan]] Fumo Bakari fled. Witu was absorbed into the [[s:east-africa-protectorate|East Africa Protectorate]], and the sultanate was formally ended in 1923.

wajo-kingdom.t: A Bugis kingdom of South Sulawesi with an elected ruler and a famous tradition of freedom, whose merchants traded across the archipelago.
wajo-kingdom.o: Wajo grew in the 15th century around [[e:tosora|Tosora]] on [[e:lake-tempe|Lake Tempe]], from a union of farming communities. Its chronicles describe a founding agreement between ruler and people that guaranteed the people's freedoms, summed up in the saying that the people of Wajo are free and only custom is their master.
wajo-kingdom.r: Wajo's head, the [[e:arung-matoa|Arung Matoa]], was elected by a council of lords and could be removed. [[e:la-tadampare-puang-ri-magalatung|La Tadampare Puang ri Ma'galatung]], in the 16th century, is remembered as its wisest ruler. In 1582 Wajo joined Bone and [[s:soppeng-kingdom|Soppeng]] in the Tellumpoccoe, but in 1610 Gowa conquered it and imposed [[e:islam|Islam]]. Wajo merchants built networks from [[s:johor-sultanate|Johor]] to [[e:sumbawa|Sumbawa]].
wajo-kingdom.e: Wajo backed Gowa in the war of 1666 to 1669 and suffered when Gowa lost. In the 18th century [[e:la-maddukelleng|La Maddukelleng]] returned from exile in [[e:borneo|Borneo]] to fight Bone and the [[e:dutch|Dutch]]. The Dutch conquered Wajo in 1906, and it is now a regency of South [[e:sulawesi|Sulawesi]].

weimar-republic.t: Germany's first parliamentary democracy, born of defeat in 1918 and destroyed by depression and the rise of the Nazis.
weimar-republic.o: The [[s:german-empire|German Empire]] collapsed in November 1918 with naval mutinies and revolution. On 9 November [[e:philipp-scheidemann|Philipp Scheidemann]] proclaimed a republic in [[e:berlin|Berlin]] as [[e:wilhelm-ii|William II]] abdicated. A national assembly met in [[e:weimar|Weimar]] to avoid unrest in the capital and adopted a democratic constitution in August 1919, with [[e:friedrich-ebert|Friedrich Ebert]] as president.
weimar-republic.r: The republic faced the [[e:treaty-of-versailles|Treaty of Versailles]], the [[e:kapp-putsch|Kapp Putsch]], political murders and the hyperinflation of 1923, when the French occupied the [[e:ruhr|Ruhr]]. Under [[e:gustav-stresemann|Gustav Stresemann]] it stabilised, joined the [[e:league-of-nations|League of Nations]] and saw a cultural flowering in [[e:berlin|Berlin]], from the [[e:bauhaus|Bauhaus]] to cinema. The [[e:great-depression|Great Depression]] brought mass unemployment and rule by emergency decree from 1930.
weimar-republic.e: President [[e:paul-von-hindenburg|Paul von Hindenburg]] appointed [[e:adolf-hitler|Adolf Hitler]] chancellor on 30 January 1933. The [[e:reichstag-fire-decree|Reichstag Fire Decree]] of February 1933 and the [[e:enabling-act-of-1933|Enabling Act]] of March 1933 destroyed parliamentary rule, ending the republic and beginning [[s:nazi-germany|Nazi Germany]].

western-guo.t: A Ji-clan state that moved from the Wei valley to the Yellow River, leaving the rich Guo cemetery at Sanmenxia, and fell to Jin in the famous ruse of the borrowed road.
western-guo.o: Western [[e:guo-state|Guo]] was founded by a brother of [[e:king-wen-of-zhou|King Wen of Zhou]] near [[e:baoji|Baoji]] in the [[e:wei-river|Wei River]] valley. Around the end of the [[s:western-zhou|Western Zhou]], its rulers moved east to Shangyang, near modern [[e:sanmenxia|Sanmenxia]] in [[e:henan|Henan]], controlling a key crossing on the [[e:yellow-river|Yellow River]].
western-guo.r: The dukes of [[e:guo-state|Guo]] were senior ministers at the Zhou court and led royal campaigns into the 7th century BCE. The [[e:shangcunling-cemetery|Shangcunling cemetery]] at [[e:sanmenxia|Sanmenxia]], with [[e:chariot|chariot]] pits and the tomb of Guo Ji containing jade burial garments and one of [[e:china|China's]] earliest iron-bladed swords, shows the state's wealth.
western-guo.e: In 655 BCE [[e:duke-xian-of-jin|Duke Xian of Jin]], having bribed the [[s:state-of-yu|State of Yu]] to let his army pass, captured Shangyang and ended [[e:guo-state|Guo]], then destroyed Yu on the way home. The episode gave Chinese the idiom 'borrowing a road to destroy Guo'.

west-indies-federation.t: Britain's attempt to lead its Caribbean colonies to independence as one nation, which broke up after only four years when Jamaica voted to leave.
west-indies-federation.o: Discussions on federation began at [[e:montego-bay|Montego Bay]] in 1947. The [[e:west-indies|West Indies]] Federation came into being on 3 January 1958, joining ten British territories: [[s:jamaica|Jamaica]], [[s:trinidad-and-tobago|Trinidad and Tobago]], [[s:barbados|Barbados]], the [[e:leeward-islands|Leeward Islands]] of [[s:colony-of-antigua|Antigua]], [[s:saint-christopher-nevis-anguilla|Saint Kitts-Nevis-Anguilla]] and [[s:montserrat|Montserrat]], and the [[e:windward-islands|Windward Islands]] of [[s:grenada|Grenada]], [[e:saint-vincent-island|Saint Vincent]], [[s:saint-lucia|Saint Lucia]] and [[s:commonwealth-of-dominica|Dominica]].
west-indies-federation.r: The federal government, led by Prime Minister [[e:grantley-adams|Grantley Adams]] of [[s:barbados|Barbados]] with [[e:patrick-buchan-hepburn-1st-baron-hailes|Lord Hailes]] as governor-general, sat in [[e:port-of-spain|Port of Spain]], as the chosen capital site at [[e:chaguaramas|Chaguaramas]] was a US base. It had a small budget, no power over income tax and no [[e:customs-union|customs union]]. [[s:jamaica|Jamaica]] and [[e:trinidad|Trinidad]], the largest members, feared paying for the small islands and disagreed over free movement of people.
west-indies-federation.e: Jamaicans voted to leave in a referendum in September 1961, and [[e:eric-williams|Eric Williams]] declared that 'one from ten leaves nought'. The federation was dissolved on 31 May 1962. Shared institutions such as the University of the [[e:west-indies|West Indies]] and the West Indies cricket team survived, and [[e:caribbean-community|CARICOM]] later revived regional cooperation.

white-horde.t: The eastern wing of the Golden Horde, ruled by descendants of Jochi's son Orda on the steppes of Kazakhstan.
white-horde.o: After Jochi, [[e:genghis-khan|Genghis Khan's]] eldest son, died in 1227, his lands were divided. His eldest son [[e:orda-khan|Orda]] received the eastern part, the left wing of the ulus, east of the [[e:ural-river|Ural River]], with its own line of khans subordinate to the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]]. Names of the 'White' and 'Blue' wings are used inconsistently in the sources.
white-horde.r: The khans of the [[e:orda-khan|Orda]] line ruled nomadic Turkic and Mongol tribes in the steppes of the [[e:syr-darya|Syr Darya]] and the [[e:irtysh|Irtysh]], with towns such as [[e:sighnaq|Sighnaq]] and [[e:sauran|Sauran]] on the Syr Darya. The Orda khans enjoyed considerable autonomy and sent their own envoys to the Yuan and Ilkhanid courts.
white-horde.e: In 1378 [[e:tokhtamysh|Tokhtamysh]], backed by [[e:timur|Timur]], made himself khan of the White Horde, and by 1380 he had seized [[e:sarai|Sarai]] and reunited it with the rest of the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]]. After further civil wars the eastern lands passed to [[e:shaybanids|Shibanid]] and other [[e:jochids|Jochid]] princes, notably [[e:abul-khayr-khan|Abu'l-Khayr]] of the [[s:uzbek-khanate|Uzbek Khanate]] in 1428.

white-croats.t: A shadowy Slavic people north of the Carpathians, named by a Byzantine emperor as the homeland of the Croats of the Adriatic.
white-croats.o: The Byzantine emperor [[e:constantine-vii|Constantine VII]] wrote in the 10th century of a White or unbaptised [[e:croatia|Croatia]] beyond [[e:hungary|Hungary]], from which some [[e:croats|Croats]] had migrated to [[e:dalmatia|Dalmatia]] in the 7th century. Historians usually place the White Croats on the upper [[e:dniester|Dniester]] and [[e:vistula|Vistula]], on both slopes of the [[e:carpathian-mountains|Carpathians]], but their exact territory is disputed.
white-croats.r: Very little is known of their society. They appear to have lived in fortified hill settlements, such as the large site at [[e:stilsko|Stilsko]] near [[e:lviv|Lviv]], and to have farmed and herded in the Carpathian foothills. The [[e:primary-chronicle|Primary Chronicle]] lists [[e:croats|Croats]] among the [[e:east-slavs|East Slavic]] tribes who took part in Oleg's campaign against [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]] in 907.
white-croats.e: In 992 Vladimir I of [[s:kievan-rus|Kievan Rus']] campaigned against the [[e:croats|Croats]], and they disappear from the sources soon afterwards. Their eastern lands became part of Rus' and later the [[s:principality-of-galicia|Principality of Galicia]], while the western parts around [[e:krakow|Krakow]] passed to the [[s:duchy-of-poland|Duchy of Poland]].

weihaiwei.t: A British naval leased territory on the Shandong coast, a quiet backwater ruled by scholar-commissioners until its return to China in 1930.
weihaiwei.o: In 1898, after [[e:russia|Russia]] leased [[e:lushunkou|Port Arthur]], [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] obtained Weihaiwei from the [[s:qing-empire|Qing Empire]] on a lease to last as long as Russia held Port Arthur. It served as a summer anchorage for the [[e:royal-navy|Royal Navy's]] [[e:china|China]] Station, with a base on [[e:liugong-island|Liugong]] island.
weihaiwei.r: After a brief military administration, a civil commissioner governed from Port Edward. The territory was never developed into a major port or base, and British rule was light, working through village headmen and Chinese custom. Its commissioners included the scholar-administrators [[e:james-stewart-lockhart|James Stewart Lockhart]] and [[e:reginald-johnston|Reginald Johnston]], former tutor to the last Qing emperor, [[e:puyi|Puyi]].
weihaiwei.e: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] agreed to return Weihaiwei at the [[e:washington-naval-conference|Washington Conference]] of 1922, and it was handed to the [[s:nationalist-government|Nationalist government]] on 1 October 1930, while the [[e:royal-navy|Royal Navy]] kept the use of [[e:liugong-island|Liugong]] island facilities for some years more.

wilusa.t: Wilusa, a kingdom of north-western Anatolia in Hittite texts, widely identified with Homer's Troy and its city of Ilios.
wilusa.o: Wilusa appears in Hittite records from the 15th century BCE, first as part of the [[s:assuwa|Assuwa]] league. Most scholars identify it with [[e:troy|Troy]] at Hisarlik, guarding the entrance to the [[e:hellespont|Dardanelles]], whose sixth and seventh cities were large walled citadels with a lower town.
wilusa.r: Its kings ruled as [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[s:hittite-empire|Hittite Empire]]. Around 1280 BCE [[e:muwatalli-ii|Muwatalli II]] made a treaty with [[e:alaksandu|Alaksandu]] of Wilusa, whose name resembles Alexandros, [[e:homer|Homer's]] [[e:paris|Paris]], and the treaty invokes a god [[e:appaliuna|Appaliuna]]. Later letters show the Mycenaean king of [[s:ahhiyawa|Ahhiyawa]] contesting control of Wilusa and the deposition of a king named [[e:walmu|Walmu]].
wilusa.e: [[e:troy|Troy]] VIIa was destroyed by fire around 1180 BCE, at the end of the [[e:late-bronze-age|Late Bronze Age]], and Wilusa vanishes from written sources. Greek epic transformed its memory into the story of the [[e:trojan-war|Trojan War]].

western-liang-555-587.t: A small client state around Jiangling on the middle Yangtze, where a branch of the Liang imperial family reigned under Western Wei, Northern Zhou and Sui protection.
western-liang-555-587.o: In 554 [[s:western-wei|Western Wei]] armies captured [[e:jiangling|Jiangling]] and killed [[e:emperor-yuan-of-liang|Emperor Yuan of Liang]]. The following year they installed his nephew [[e:xiao-cha|Xiao Cha]], a grandson of [[e:emperor-wu-of-han|Emperor Wu]] of the [[s:liang-dynasty|Liang dynasty]] and a rival of the Jiangling court, as emperor of a rump [[s:liang-liang-shidu|Liang]] state confined to the district around the city.
western-liang-555-587.r: Its emperors kept the full ceremony of a Chinese court, with reign titles and officials, but a [[s:western-wei|Western Wei]] and later [[s:northern-zhou|Northern Zhou]] garrison stood in [[e:jiangling|Jiangling]], and the rulers depended entirely on their northern patrons. The territory was only a few prefectures wide. [[e:xiao-kui|Xiao Kui]], the second emperor, was a respected scholar, and his daughter married [[e:emperor-yang-of-sui|Yang Guang]], the future Emperor Yang of the [[s:sui-dynasty|Sui Dynasty]].
western-liang-555-587.e: In 587 [[e:emperor-wen-of-sui|Emperor Wen of Sui]] summoned the third ruler, [[e:xiao-cong|Xiao Cong]], to [[e:changan|Chang'an]] and abolished the state; some of its officials fled to the [[s:chen-dynasty|Chen dynasty]]. The Xiao family remained prominent under [[e:sui-dynasty|Sui]] and [[s:later-tang|Tang]] thanks to the marriage tie.

west-jersey.t: A Quaker colony on the Delaware River whose 1677 Concessions and Agreements set out some of the most liberal rights of any 17th-century government.
west-jersey.o: In 1674 [[e:john-berkeley-1st-baron-berkeley-of-stratton|Lord Berkeley]] sold his half of [[e:new-jersey|New Jersey]] to the [[e:quakers|Quakers]] [[e:john-fenwick-quaker|John Fenwick]] and [[e:edward-byllynge|Edward Byllynge]], and [[e:william-penn|William Penn]] became a trustee for the debt-ridden Byllynge. Fenwick founded Salem in 1675, and in 1677 a shipload of Quakers founded [[e:burlington-new-jersey|Burlington]], which became the capital. The [[e:quintipartite-deed|Quintipartite Deed]] of 1676 separated West [[s:bailiwick-of-jersey|Jersey]] from [[s:east-jersey|East Jersey]].
west-jersey.r: The Concessions and Agreements of 1677, associated with [[e:william-penn|Penn]], guaranteed freedom of conscience, [[e:jury-trial|trial by jury]] and an elected assembly with wide powers. [[e:quakers|Quaker]] meetings shaped community life, and the colony served as a model for the [[s:province-of-pennsylvania|Province of Pennsylvania]]. Farmers along the [[e:delaware-river|Delaware]] raised grain and livestock. After [[e:edward-byllynge|Byllynge]]'s death the physician [[e:daniel-coxe|Daniel Coxe]] bought the governing rights in 1687 and sold them to the West [[s:bailiwick-of-jersey|Jersey]] Society in 1692.
west-jersey.e: Disputes between proprietors and settlers led to the surrender of government in 1702, reuniting West and [[s:east-jersey|East Jersey]] as the royal [[s:province-of-new-jersey|Province of New Jersey]]. The Council of Proprietors of West [[s:bailiwick-of-jersey|Jersey]] still meets in [[e:burlington-new-jersey|Burlington]].

willoughbyland.t: An English sugar colony on the Suriname river, founded from Barbados, that was lost to the Dutch in 1667 in exchange for New York.
willoughbyland.o: In 1650 Francis, [[e:francis-willoughby-5th-baron-willoughby-of-parham|Lord Willoughby of Parham]], the royalist governor of [[s:barbados|Barbados]], sent Anthony Rowse with settlers to the [[s:suriname|Suriname]] river in [[e:guianas|Guiana]]. In 1652 Willoughby visited the colony, and in 1662 he received a royal grant from [[e:charles-ii-of-england|Charles II]]. The capital was [[e:torarica|Torarica]], a small town on the river.
willoughbyland.r: Willoughbyland grew quickly to several thousand people, with some fifty [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] plantations worked by enslaved Africans. [[e:sephardic-jews|Sephardic Jewish]] settlers, some from [[s:dutch-brazil|Dutch Brazil]], were granted privileges and founded settlements along the river that later became [[e:jodensavanne|Jodensavanne]]. The writer [[e:aphra-behn|Aphra Behn]] claimed to have lived there and set her novel [[e:oroonoko|Oroonoko]] in the colony. A governor ruled with an assembly of planters.
willoughbyland.e: In 1667, during the [[e:second-anglo-dutch-war|Second Anglo-Dutch War]], a [[s:county-of-zeeland|Zeeland]] fleet under [[e:abraham-crijnssen|Abraham Crijnssen]] captured the colony. The [[e:treaty-of-breda-1667|Treaty of Breda]] that year confirmed [[e:dutch|Dutch]] possession of [[s:suriname|Suriname]] in exchange for [[e:england|England]] keeping [[s:new-netherland|New Netherland]], renamed [[e:new-york|New York]]. Many English planters left by 1680.

west-breifne.t: The O'Rourke lordship of Leitrim, heir to the old kingdom of Breifne, which lasted until the Elizabethan and Jacobean conquest.
west-breifne.o: When the [[s:kingdom-of-breifne|Kingdom of Breifne]] split in 1256, the [[e:o-ruairc|O'Rourkes]] held the western part, roughly modern [[e:county-leitrim|County Leitrim]], while the [[e:o-raghallaigh|O'Reillys]] took the east. [[e:dromahair|Dromahair]], by [[e:lough-gill|Lough Gill]], became the O'Rourke seat.
west-breifne.r: West Breifne was a land of small lakes, hills and [[e:cattle|cattle]]-raising, ruled through Gaelic law with bardic and learned families. The [[e:o-ruairc|O'Rourkes]] founded [[e:creevelea-friary|Creevelea Friary]] in 1508. [[e:brian-orourke|Brian O'Rourke]] sheltered [[e:spanish-armada|Spanish Armada]] survivors in 1588 and was executed at [[e:tyburn|Tyburn]] in 1591 for treason.
west-breifne.e: His son Brian Og fought with [[e:hugh-oneill-earl-of-tyrone|O'Neill]] in the [[e:nine-years-war-ireland|Nine Years' War]]. After defeat the lordship was shired as [[e:county-leitrim|County Leitrim]] and, in the early 17th century, planted with English settlers within the [[s:kingdom-of-ireland|Kingdom of Ireland]].
